newsitem.title: BELGIUM: City Hotels to launch airline March 27.
newsitem.headline: City Hotels to launch airline March 27.

text.p: Belgian hotel and leisure group City Hotels said in a statement on Monday it would launch its planned City Bird long-haul airline on March 27.
Operating a McDonnell Douglas MD-11 aircraft, City Bird will offer, via Belgian travel group Neckermann, flights from Brussels to the Dominican Republic, Cuba, Mexico, Jamaica.
It will also run regular services to Miami, Orlando and Mexico City, City Hotels said in a statement on 1996 results.
City Bird would take delivery of a second MD-11 at the beginning of June and extend its services to Los Angeles, San Francisco and New York, City Hotels said.
Each MD-11 would be divided into a 36-seat first class section and a 335-seat economy class, City Hotels said.

"The pricing policy will be the same as that which made EBA a success: permanently low prices and no restrictions (no minimum stays, no required weekend stops, no maximum ages...)," City Hotels said, referring to its EuroBelgian Airline (EBA) unit sold to the Virgin Group last year.

City Bird's first class seats would be sold at approximately 40 percent less than traditional airlines' business class seats, it said. "City Bird aims to rapidly become Belgium's premier long-haul airline," it added.
City Hotels said City Bird currently employs 110 people. It said this will rise to 180 with the delivery of the second MD-11 in June.
